title: Letter shapes: how letters join (and the six that don't)

bigIdea.text: Inside a word, Arabic letters hold hands, so most letters change shape a little depending on where they stand. Six letters never hold the hand of the letter after them.

proper.text: A letter can have four forms: isolated (alone), initial (at the start of a joined piece), medial (in the middle) and final (at the end). Mostly the joining stroke changes; the core shape and the dots stay the same.
Six letters join only to the letter before them, never to the letter after: ا د ذ ر ز و. After one of them the next letter starts fresh, in its initial form (or isolated, if it is the last letter).
So a gap inside a word does not start a new word. A gap after ا د ذ ر ز و is part of the same word; the space between two words is wider.

Some joining letters change a lot: ه looks quite different at the start, middle and end; ع and غ are an open cup at the start but closed in the middle and at the end; ك loses the small mark inside it when another letter follows. Trust the dots and the core shape.
When ل is followed by ا, the two fuse into one special shape called lam-alif. Read it as lam, then alif.

visual.caption: The six non-joiners: they take a hand from the right, never give one to the left.

memoryHook.text: Six never reach left: ا د ذ ر ز و.

extras.text: The thin joining line is called tatweel (or kashida). Calligraphers stretch it for beauty; it never changes the sound.
Persian/Urdu readers: the same six letters refuse to join forward in your script too (Persian adds ژ). Your eyes already know this pattern.

note.text: One word, two breaks: د and و never join the letter after them.
Breaks after the alif (with its hamza) and after و; ع takes its initial form after the first break.
Five pieces in one word: breaks after ٱ, after each و and after ا.
After ٱ the rest is one joined piece; look for ع in its middle form.
ه in its initial form, joined to a final و.
و stands alone, then ل and ا fuse into lam-alif.

drills.prompt: Say the six non-joiners by name: alif, dal, dhal, ra, zay, waw (ا د ذ ر ز و).
Read these joined pairs slowly and notice the break after the second letter: بَدَ · بَرَ · بَوَ · بَزَ

tip.text: Same shape, one dot apart. د: tongue tip on the gum ridge (a 'd'). ذ: tongue tip lightly between the teeth, voiced like 'th' in 'this'. Neither joins forward.

questions.q: Which group lists exactly the six letters that never join the letter after them?
options: ا د ذ ر ز و
ا ب ت ث ج ح
د ذ ر ز س ش
ا د ر و ي ن
explain: Right: alif, dal, dhal, ra, zay and waw.
ب ت ث ج ح join on both sides; only the alif belongs to the six.
س and ش join on both sides.
ي and ن join on both sides.

questions.q: A word on screen has a small gap right after a ر. What does the gap mean?
options: Nothing special: ر never joins forward, so the same word goes on
A new word starts after the gap
explain: Right: gaps after the six non-joiners are normal inside a word.
Words are separated by a wider space; this gap is inside the word.
Pauses are shown by pause signs, not by gaps.
The ر is read as usual; it just doesn't join forward.

questions.q: In which form does a letter join on BOTH sides?
explain: Right: in the middle it joins the letter before and the letter after.
Alone it joins nothing.
At the start of a piece it joins only the letter after it.
At the end it joins only the letter before it.

questions.q: Inside a word, a letter comes right after a د. Which form does that letter take?
options: Initial (or isolated if it is the last letter)
explain: Right: د does not join forward, so the next letter starts fresh.
Medial needs a joining letter before it; د cannot give that join.
Final means joined to the letter before, which د does not allow.
Every letter is written and read; nothing is hidden.

questions.q: Do a letter's dots change when it joins other letters?
options: No: the dots stay the same in every form
Yes: they move below the line
Yes: joined letters lose their dots
Only at the end of a word
explain: Right: only the joining strokes change; the dots tell you the letter.
Dots stay where they are (above or below).
Dots are kept; without them ب ت ث ن ي could not be told apart.
Dots are the same at the start, middle and end.

questions.q: Which set of letters would be written as ONE unbroken shape, in this order?
explain: Right: all four are joiners, so they link up into one piece.
ا does not join forward, so the second ب starts a new piece.
و does not join forward, so ن starts a new piece.
ر does not join forward, so د stands apart.

questions.q: Which letter joins the letter before it but NOT the letter after it?
explain: Right: zay is one of the six non-joiners.
sin joins on both sides.
lam joins on both sides.
mim joins on both sides.

questions.q: How many forms can a joining letter like ب have?
explain: Right.
Size is not what changes; the joins do.
Forms depend on the position in the word, not on height.
Joining letters change their joining strokes.

questions.q: Inside a word, a ب comes right after an ا. Which form is that ب in?
options: Initial (or isolated if it is the last letter)
explain: Right: alif never joins forward, so ب starts a new piece.
Medial would need a join from the alif.
Alif cannot join the letter after it.
The ب is written and read normally.

questions.q: Which statement about gaps inside a word is true?
options: A gap after ا د ذ ر ز و is normal inside one word
Every gap means a new word
A gap means a long vowel
A gap is a pause sign
explain: Right.
Only the wider space separates words.
Long vowels come from madd letters, not from gaps.
Pause signs are small marks above the line.

questions.q: Which pair is told apart only by a dot, in every form?
explain: Right: same shape; zay has one dot above.
و has a round head; ر does not.
د is angular and sits on the line; ر curves below it.
ا is a straight stroke; و has a round head.

questions.q: In which form does a letter join ONLY the letter before it?
explain: Right: at the end of a piece it takes a hand from the right only.
Initial joins only the letter after it.
Medial joins both sides.
Isolated joins nothing.

questions.q: Why do ا د ذ ر ز و so often end a joined piece of a word?
options: Because they cannot join forward, so the piece stops after them
Because they are always long vowels
Because a pause always follows them
explain: Right.
They are pronounced like any other letter.
Only ا and و can be long vowels, and that is not about joining.
Pauses are shown by pause signs, not by letters.

remnote: Letters that never join the next letter == ا د ذ ر ز و (alif, dal, dhal, ra, zay, waw)
The four letter forms == Isolated, initial, medial, final
A gap after ا د ذ ر ز و inside a word == Same word: those six simply don't join forward
Do dots change when letters join? == No, only the joining strokes change
ل followed by ا == They fuse into one shape, lam-alif
